Rules.Title: Purpose & Scope
Content: Authority defines how the active run context is interpreted: which rule layers take precedence, how current state and user corrections are reconciled, and how a fresh AI instance should treat the supplied handoff. It does not define ordinary gameplay strategy.

Rules.Title: Layer Precedence
Content: Authority sits outside ordinary gameplay precedence because it defines what the included layers mean. Bootstrap Truth applies only while reconstructing usable context. During normal play, more specific Truth layers override less specific ones when they directly conflict: Custom Truth overrides Preferences Truth, Preferences Truth overrides Game Truth, and Game Truth overrides Core Truth. For player-facing rules, Custom Instructions override conflicting Game Instructions, Game Instructions override conflicting Core Instructions, and Runtime Instructions form the active execution surface for the selected character. Rules that do not conflict remain cumulative.

Rules.Title: Package Authority
Content: game-companion.json is the portable handoff for the selected run. Its contents are authoritative for the snapshot they represent. Exported character state is authoritative for every field it successfully captures, while rule layers govern interpretation, decisions, and execution rather than replacing live state.

Rules.Title: Freshness & User Reports
Content: If a newer explicit user report conflicts with an older exported snapshot, treat the export as stale for that fact and reason from the newest reliable information until refreshed state is available. Do not force an immediate refresh solely to verify every low-risk or reversible report. Exact rolls, requirements, hidden state, or other missing details that materially affect a decision remain unknown until established by refreshed state, reliable research, or user observation.

Rules.Title: Missing State
Content: A missing, incomplete, or unhandled exported field is not proof that the underlying item, stat, resource, or game state is absent. Preserve material uncertainty and resolve it through reliable research or user observation when the next decision depends on it.

Rules.Title: User Corrections
Content: An explicit user correction to known state is authoritative for the current interaction. Do not continue reasoning from a value the user has explicitly identified as stale or wrong.

Rules.Title: Source Conflicts
Content: When authoritative information conflicts, apply layer precedence and freshness rather than silently merging incompatible values. Preserve a material unresolved conflict explicitly until it can be resolved.

Rules.Title: Runtime Instructions
Content: Runtime Instructions are the active execution surface for the selected character. They contain the current task package and, when applicable, permanent stopping conditions, review queues, immediate execution queues, manual tracking criteria, game-specific watchlists, and temporary manual-state bridges. Anything the user must execute, watch for, stop for, report, preserve, or otherwise act on should be surfaced there.

Rules.Title: Journey
Content: Journey contains durable tactical findings that explain how the selected character is currently played, such as Current Skill Doctrine, Current Boss Doctrine, or game-appropriate equivalents. Current physical and progression state belongs to exported character state rather than being duplicated in Journey.
